note: Every entry below was checked against the vendor documentation linked in its docs field on the last_reviewed date. Bucket assignment is the load bearing part of the score, not the user agent string. obeys_robots records whether the vendor documents the agent as honouring robots.txt: yes, no, or disputed. An agent that does not honour robots.txt cannot be blocked there, and the report says so instead of pretending the block worked.

buckets.citation: Feeds retrieval and citation in AI answers. Blocking these removes the site from AI results. Worth 50 points of the Access score. ai_only marks the ones that exist only to feed AI answers. Googlebot and Bingbot also carry classic search, so blocking them is a bigger and different story.
buckets.user_fetch: Fetches a page on demand when a user pastes a link or asks about it. Worth 20 points of the Access score.
buckets.training: Collects pages for model training. Worth zero points. Reported as posture, never penalised.

agents.note: Powers ChatGPT search. Blocking this removes the site from ChatGPT results, which is what most people get wrong. GPTBot is the training crawler and is a different thing entirely.
Improves search result quality for Claude users.
Surfaces and links websites in Perplexity results. Documented as not used for foundation model training.
Feeds Google Search, and AI Overviews are built from that index. Separate from Google-Extended, which does not affect Search.
Grounds Microsoft Copilot, and ChatGPT search also draws on the Bing index.
Powers Spotlight, Siri and Safari search. Also feeds Apple foundation models unless Applebot-Extended is disallowed.
Fetches a page when a ChatGPT user asks about it. OpenAI documents that robots.txt rules may not apply to these user initiated fetches.
Fetches a page when a Claude user asks about it. Documented as honouring robots.txt.
Perplexity documents that this fetcher generally ignores robots.txt rules. Disallowing it here does not stop the fetch.
On demand fetch for Le Chat. Not used for training.
Fetches individual links at a user's request. Meta documents that it may bypass robots.txt for user initiated requests.
Training only. Blocking it does not affect ChatGPT search citations.
Legacy token, no longer listed in Anthropic documentation but still present in many robots.txt files.
Gemini training and grounding. Google documents that it does not affect Search inclusion or ranking.
Opt out control for Apple foundation model training. Pages that disallow it still appear in Apple search.
Feeds an open crawl archive used by many downstream training datasets.
Trains Meta foundation models and indexes content directly.
Builds datasets for Mistral generative models.
ByteDance claims robots.txt compliance but the reference URL is unreachable outside China, and independent measurements report it fetching disallowed pages. Treated as disputed.
Improves Amazon products and trains Amazon AI models. Amzn-SearchBot is the separate search crawler.
Collects web content for Cohere enterprise model training. Cohere publishes no dedicated crawler page.
Sells structured web data onward for AI training and retrieval, so one block covers many downstream consumers.
Being replaced by webzio-extended. Both still appear in the wild.
Successor token to omgilibot, specifically for AI training data.
